text:
Round 314 — corrected decode measurement ledger and next CPU pool axis
Date: 2026-10-13 (JST)
Status: read-only review of already closed committed result directories, source contracts, and prior reports. No active Main receipt/log read, benchmark/test/build, GPU/profiler/model/process action, Git operation, cleanup, or source edit. Main's qualified GEN128 controller/run is still independently owned; no action here interrupts it.

## Finding

R311 is superseded on paired-GU evidence by the already completed CPU qualification: `iq3s_paired_gu_test` passes for flag 0/1 in both free and contrib-LLVM builds, including all 640 rows and scalar/gather variants, and the isolated single-thread synthetic NT1 paired path is about 3.8% faster. It remains OFF because this narrow synthetic component result has no corresponding production model-arm result, the gain is small relative to natural timing variation, and the routed type21/NT1 job denominator is unknown. R311's claim that no completed parity fixture or component timing was found is therefore outdated. Its warning that no paired model/runtime performance result exists remains correct.

The closed decode diagnostic supplies a substantially better path ledger than R311 used, but it is diagnostic-only and has nested host intervals. The next concrete, independent, reversible axis is CPU pool task grain after Main closes its current GEN128 work: with worker count fixed to the owner-selected stable arm (or existing five-worker default if that screen still cannot separate arms), compare `--pool-tasks 6`, `18`, and `24` in matched fresh-process 32,768-input + 128-output runs. This tests one task-grain factor without repeating the paired-GU suggestion or the just-completed 3/4/5-worker screen. Keep all route/model/cache/PCIe/MTP/prefill/affinity/math settings constant. No task count is presumed better.

## Closed decode ledger and evidence scope

The committed `2026-10-12-decode-criticalpath-native-dequant-batch/README.md` and `results.json` record Arc B570 10 GiB / Ryzen 5 5600X, free LLVM 7.1.1, source 0691bcdf, configured context 262,144, actual input 32,768, 16 output tokens, G16, 8,192 prompt chunk, cache 144 slots, and five CPU workers. The diagnostic line is:

`strata decode timing: 16 windows, avg T 1.00, 1.00 tokens/window, 124.09 ms/window = verify 121.44 (GPU-reach wait 50.27 + per-layer host 55.16 [plan 0.05 actq 0.07 jobs 0.04 CPU 50.64] + stage 0.49) + commit/emit 2.65 + draft 0.00; per layer-window: CPU experts 9.45 (9.45 entries), VRAM hits 0.55, PCIe 0.00; before the window 0.00, adapt join 0.00 (adapt 0.00, 0 swaps, 0 synchronous)`.

That line provides these measured request-level facts: average of 9.45 CPU experts and 9.45 routed entries per layer-window, 0.55 VRAM hits, zero PCIe experts, and the named nested host spans. It is not an exclusive CPU/GPU equation; do not add the wait, host, stage and CPU fields to claim elapsed critical path or CPU cycles. The receipt marks the native diagnostic as validation-overhead data and performance-ineligible; it is not a clean performance baseline. The separate three clean OFF/ON prefill-batch pairs give 8.10 vs 8.27 mean decode tok/s with identical 16 token/LP5 outputs, but decode computation was unchanged, and the committed report explicitly forbids attributing that variation to the prefill-only flag.

The missing production denominator is **per layer/window, CPU-owned job count bucketed by `(GU type, Down type, NT)`**, including exact type21/NT1 count and, if attributing pool tails, per-worker rows/jobs completed or active/wait timing. `CPU experts 9.45` is only an overall average, not the number of IQ3_S experts; mean T=1 and entries=distinct jobs imply one token per decode window but the printed aggregate does not certify a type-specific histogram. The native diagnostic group sums (10,096 GU and Down admissions each, 93,525 covered-row counts each, no fallback/decline) likewise aggregate the supported format/NT cells and do not expose the type/NT distribution. Therefore the paired-GU result cannot be multiplied by a measured type21 share, and the current request counters cannot distinguish imbalance from CPU kernel service, claim/barrier wait, or caller/worker partition.

The qualified outputs for the six worker-screen samples are a closed but low-repetition screen: workers 5/3/4/4/3/5, `pool-tasks=18`, two samples each, 32K + 16. Means are 2,183.7 ms decode at five workers, 2,185.95 ms at three, and 2,114.9 ms at four, but the two four-worker samples span 1,744.3–2,485.5 ms. All six passed exact token/LP5, no-fresh-fault, and normal-close checks; none was promoted. This spread is why worker count remains unresolved and why the same screen should not be repeated at 16 tokens. Main's current GEN128 work is the right next owner for longer decode validation. The proposed task-grain screen is conditional on that work closing and holding a chosen worker arm fixed.

## Paired IQ3_S GU evidence that corrects R311

The committed `2026-10-12-avx2-expert-roofline-and-paired-gu/README.md` and `cpu-kernel-results.json` cover 256 MiB of valid synthetic native-quantized expert data, H=2560, FF=640, one thread pinned to CPU 0, five raw repetitions per cell, and pre-quantized activations. The engine-dispatch median for IQ3_S/IQ4_NL is:

| NT | Gate/Up | Down | Sum of isolated phase medians |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 0.31858 ms | 0.09677 ms | 0.41535 ms |
| 8 | 0.84144 ms | 0.43143 ms | 1.26264 ms |

The separate paired-GU OFF/ON sweep reports NT1 means 0.31542 vs 0.30355 ms (−3.76% with flag 1); its two ON medians are 0.29594/0.31115 ms, while OFF is 0.31267/0.31817 ms. At NT8 the means are 0.87118 vs 0.89130 ms (+2.31%; no gain). This is a synthetic one-thread component test—not a pool or model result, and not repeated production route weighting. Gather NT1 is +17.57% slower on this 5600X sample, so it is not an alternate decode recommendation. Paired parity passes are exact bit parity of fixture output across 640 rows, four production-quantized activation patterns, scalar/gather, range partitions/rejection canaries; two compiler build modes passed. The tested fixture uses synthetic weight bytes, has no runtime/model output evidence, and does not substitute for ASan/UBSan or model correctness unless those separate recorded checks are explicitly called out. `README.md` reports free and contrib-LLVM engine/test builds and ASan/UBSan passed with all expected items enabled. The flag remains default OFF, and no paired model runtime was run.

The 0.319 ms GU and 0.097 ms Down estimates cannot be multiplied by 9.45 jobs/layer to predict model time: the model pools work over workers/caller, shares one quantized activation across duplicate route entries, and has concurrent GPU/boundary work. The aggregate counts give neither format exposure nor job/service distribution. The result supports continuing only as a small optional component hypothesis if exact production routing later shows enough eligible work.

## Why task grain is the next one-axis screen

At `pool.cpp:409-410`, task count 0 means three tasks per participating thread; an explicit positive `--pool-tasks N` caps at phase rows. `generate.cpp:4079-4084` reports requested tasks and participating threads at startup. In the measured worker screen, five workers plus the decode caller means six participants and 18 automatic tasks per phase, matching the fixed comparison baseline. `run_split_multi_native` flattens eligible GU and Down rows across CPU experts (`pool.cpp:470-503`) and workers dynamically claim equal contiguous chunks. Fewer chunks reduce claims/barriers but risk a longer tail; more chunks give better redistribution opportunity but increase claim overhead and split row ranges further. No existing current-run worker idle/active distribution resolves which cost dominates.

After the existing GEN128 run closes, one concise candidate is a three-arm task count comparison: 6 (one task per six participants), 18 (screen baseline), 24 (four per participant). Freeze the best stable worker count selected by that closed GEN128 evidence; if no worker arm separates, retain the recipe default five workers. Use the same exact 32,768 input IDs and 128 output cap, model/binary/provider, cache/profile/residency, CPU affinity/host participation, MTP/spec/window behavior, PCIe share/mode, prefill settings and math flags. Interleave fresh processes; require identical generated IDs and reported LP5, normal QUIT/reap, no new GPU faults and retained failure records; compare decode wall and clean rates over at least three repetitions per arm. The 50.64 ms CPU phase may be collected only as the same diagnostic with its overhead label; it is not the acceptance metric. Keep the task candidate only if its endpoint win is repeatable and independent of output or route changes. If the variance remains wider than any arm difference, retain default and stop rather than add speculative pool/kernel changes.

This is a single CLI parameter axis, not a worker-count retest. Task counts above 24 and per-thread/pool instrumentation are not justified first. If a task-screen result is inconclusive and exact attribution is still needed, the missing low-overhead evidence should be a request-local histogram by layer, provider/CPU ownership, `(GU type, Down type, NT)` plus realized task count. A worker-imbalance claim would additionally require per-worker active/claim/wait deltas; the current aggregate timer is insufficient. Such instrumentation is a separate source change and not part of this report or present authorization.

## Primary implementation context and limits

The Strata task-grain mechanism and data layout above are source-local evidence. Intel's primary [VTune scheduling/imbalance recipe](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/vtune-profiler/cookbook/2024-1/openmp-imbalance-and-scheduling-overhead.html) states that fine dynamic chunks can trade lower imbalance for scheduling overhead and worse cache reuse. Its sample is OpenMP on Xeon, so it supports testing grain rather than any expected result on Strata/Ryzen. The [ggml-org CPU thread-pool implementation](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c) is a primary implementation comparator for dynamically claimed chunks; its work assignment, kernels and quantized model route differ, so no llama.cpp speed number is transferred.

Relevant prior reports: R270 pool/critical-path source contract; R293 IQ3_S CPU scheduling/activation reuse; R294 paired-GU eligibility and missing type/NT denominator; R311 is now corrected by the committed closed measurements above. Current report registry reviewed: `report-registry-v175.json`, 827 completed research entries, which records the latest R309/R310 updates but predates this report. Primary committed result identities include native decode `results.json`/`README.md` and worker screening `worker-screening.json`/`REPORT.md`. No completion, adoption, or performance promotion is claimed.
